scope: Method3 docs-only debate-map sentence plan; no citation binding, claim-chip binding, product/wiki publish, DB, runtime, git, cloud/API, shared-parent, or cross-method writes.
method_baseline: Start from the research-status/debate map; draft the reader-facing sentence plan before binding citations or claim chips.

debate_axes.reader_point: AGN/SMBH feedback can affect gas in scoped contexts.
AGN-associated outflow signatures appear in selected samples.
debate_axes.guard: Do not turn selected-sample or single-case results into population-wide rates.

debate_axes.reader_point: AGN feedback is one quenching axis among several.
debate_axes.guard: Do not call it the dominant cause without narrow later binding.

debate_axes.reader_point: Preventive/maintenance heating is distinct from ejective feedback.
debate_axes.guard: Do not use simulations/models as observed prevalence.

debate_axes.reader_point: Central depletion and retained reservoirs/low SFE both matter.
debate_axes.guard: Do not imply gas removal explains every quenching pathway.
Do not collapse alternatives into AGN feedback.
Do not render simulations as observed population facts.

sentence_plan.planned_reader_point: Galaxy evolution is the coupled history of stars, gas, black holes, halos, and environments.
Quenching is a central, multi-channel transition in galaxy evolution.
sentence_plan.guard: Use can involve / can be regulated by, not single-cause certainty.

sentence_plan.planned_reader_point: AGN/SMBH feedback can affect gas through jets, winds, turbulence, heating, or starvation in selected systems.
Molecular, ionized, or neutral outflows are observed in selected AGN-host or massive-galaxy samples.
Ejective/outflow feedback differs from preventive or maintenance heating.
Central depletion, retained reservoirs, and low star-formation efficiency complicate gas-removal stories.
sentence_plan.guard: Do not generalize central-kpc depletion to universal galaxy-wide gas absence.

sentence_plan.planned_reader_point: AGN feedback can matter, but dominance over other quenching channels is context-dependent and debated.
Central structure, halo/environment/satellite effects, strangulation, stripping, stellar feedback, recycling, gas retention, and low SFE remain part of the map.
Rapid shutdown in selected massive or cosmic-noon systems is important but sample- and model-dependent.
Simulations help test mechanisms and assumptions.
sentence_plan.guard: Do not present simulations as direct observed prevalence.

sentence_plan.planned_reader_point: The safest synthesis is a context-dependent, multi-channel account of quenching and galaxy evolution.
Prevalence, dominance, reservoir response, and maintenance heating remain live questions for later binding.
sentence_plan.guard: Uncertainty is a result, not a failure.
